guide.title: Agent Diagnostic Manual
guide.summary: A field guide to recognizing, distinguishing, and investigating failures in configured agents.

section.title: Overview

p.strong: ASM · Working draft · One symptom, one candidate diagnosis.

section.p: Start with what happened. Distinguish plausible explanations. Test an intervention. Keep the evidence and the uncertainty attached to the claim.

tr.td: Observable features that can occur in healthy or failing runs.
Proposed patterns with criteria, exclusions, and differential reasoning.
Conditional, testable protocols with tradeoffs and rollback.
The evidence policy; no empirical cases have been added yet.

section.title: Read the first example
section.p: An agent keeps looking up the same information. Is it checking something important, recovering from missing context, or spending its budget without advancing the task?
Follow Repeated retrieval to Unproductive repeated retrieval, then inspect Preserve task-relevant evidence. The intervention applies only when the evidence-availability hypothesis is plausible.

section.title: How this is organized
section.p: Read the XML format contract and Structure and design decisions for the source format and relationship model, and Diagnostic foundations for the distinctions behind it.

This manual describes operational behavior. It does not attribute human psychiatric conditions or subjective experiences to agents. The initial unit of assessment is an episode of a configured system: model, instructions, memory, tools, harness, and environment.
Severity scoring is deferred. Entry maturity and evidence strength are separate from severity and from confidence about any individual case.
